title: Per-request affinity and slow-path fallbacks for heterogeneous variant deploys
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Goal: implement a per-request steering and slow-path fallback mechanism that preserves low-latency for compatible model variants while safely isolating/evicting requests that hit incompatibilities or high-cost execution paths. This should reduce failed canary surface area, keep p99s stable during rollouts, and provide deterministic fallback lanes for region and capacity tier failures.

Background: current rollouts route by simple hash or session and then fall back globally when a variant is unavailable. We see two recurring problems: (1) heterogenous model variants that differ in kv-cache layout or max-seq result in soft-incompatibilities that cause runtime errors or degraded latency, and (2) cross-region spillovers cause uneven tail latencies when traffic is redirected to lower-tier capacity without an isolated slow-path.

Proposal summary:
- Add an opaque per-request affinity token (derived from request metadata and policy) so traffic can stick to warm caches and affinity queues while still supporting progressive splits.
- Define explicit slow-path lanes: CPU-hosted inference pool and pre-warmed quantized fallback variants. Requests that fail compatibility gating move to slow-path instead of failing.
- Introduce tier-aware eviction rules: prioritize maintaining primary-region low-latency paths while shedding non-critical shadow/AB traffic to best-effort tiers before autoscaling triggers.
- Implement a compatibility predicate service that runs lightweight checks (model metadata, kv keyshape, max-context) and returns a routing decision: direct, transformable, slow-path, or failover.
- Circuit-breaker and probe flow: probe shadow traffic at reduced rate to maintain coverage, and use failure rates + latency regressions to trigger auto-rollback policies with simulated rollback dry-run.

Trade-offs considered:
- Preferring slow-path over fail reduces hard errors but increases cost and tail latency for those requests; we mitigate with quota gates and cost-accounting labels.
- Affinity tokens increase routing state; we keep them opaque and encoded in a short TTL cookie so runtime stores only minimal mapping (no global sticky tables).

Design notes and API surface:
- New header: X-Rw-Affinity: base64(token) used by edge router and runtime to prefer warm slots.
- Compatibility predicate endpoint: /internal/compat-check returning one of: DIRECT | TRANSFORMABLE | SLOW_PATH | FAIL. Lightweight JSON response (internal use).
- Slow-path pools registered via runtime config: cpu-fallback, quantized-approx, remote-region-best-effort. Each pool has labels and cost-multiplier.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
1) Canary rollout of a variant that alters kv-cache layout should not elevate global 5xx rates: incompatible requests must be routed to slow-path or failover only for the affected keys.
2) End-to-end A/B experiments that include a small shadow cohort should not impact primary latency p95/p99 by >5% under baseline traffic.
3) Auto-rollback triggers when failure-rate > 1% AND p99 lateny regression > 30% for 5 minutes; rollback dry-run results must be recorded in console.
4) Affinity token TTL and routing decision logic must be visible in Console traces and per-token cost breakdowns.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Spike (1 week): prototype affinity token generator and local compat predicate simulator; run synthetic tests with models that differ by kv layout.
- Core implementation (3 weeks): runtime routing change to respect X-Rw-Affinity, slow-path pool scheduling, and compatibility predicate integration. Add metrics for token churn, slow-path hit-rate, and per-variant cost.
- Safety harness (1 week): canary gating, quota limits for slow-path, probe scheduling for shadow traffic.
- Rollout (2 weeks): staged rollout starting with internal tenants, then Canary: 1% -> 5% -> 20% with automatic rollback monitors.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for token generation, predicate outputs, and pool selection.
- Integration tests that spin up two variant models with differing cache shapes and verify requests with same affinity token hit warm slots.
- Load test to demonstrate p99 stability under 10k RPS and 10% shadow traffic.
- Chaos test: simulate region outage and validate tiered eviction moves only shadow traffic and triggers correct failover for critical routes.

Observability and alarms:
- New console charts: Affinity token distribution, Slow-path latency histogram, Slow-path cost per-token.
- Alerts: slow-path hit-rate > 2% for primary routes, compat-predicate fail > 0.5% for 10m, unexpected cross-region spillover.

Rollout / rollback plan:
- Begin in a non-customer org with synthetic traffic. If metrics good for 2 hours, promote to internal customer orgs.
- Production canary policy: 1% for 30m, 5% for 1h, 20% for 3h. Automatic rollback if any acceptance criteria breached.

Open questions:
- Should affinity tokens be derived from user identity for deterministic stickiness or purely request-scoped to avoid long-lived routing? (security/SGX considerations).
- How do we account for slow-path cost in per-customer billing? add explicit cost labels?

Notes and links:
- Prototype notes in the design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/per-request-affinity

comments: 2026-02-26 - Mateо: Spike started. Basic affinity token generator implemented. Observed 12% improvement in cache-local hits in local test harness.
2026-03-02 - Design review: listed two preferred slow-path pools (cpu-fallback + quantized-approx). Product asked for explicit billing labels on slow-path requests.
2026-03-07 - Security: flagged potential information leak if token encodes user id. Decided to keep tokens opaque and HMAC-signed; security review follow-up required.
2026-03-10 - Mateo: Implemented compat predicate stub and wired into edge; added metrics for compat decisions. Integration tests failing intermittently for cross-region probe logic.
2026-03-14 - PM Sofia: Updated acceptance criteria to include automatic rollback threshold combining failure rate and p99 regression. Added to release notes draft.
